title: Compounded Resveratrol Capsules | Empower Pharmacy
abstract:
According to one animal study, resveratrol may decrease serum levels of thyroid hormones (T3, T4) and increase levels of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in hyperthyroid-induced rats.\[[6](#footnote-6)] Per Hadi et al., the mechanism of this effect on the thyroid may involve the inhibition of sodium-iodide symporter (NIS) and antioxidant effects of resveratrol.\[[6](#footnote-6)]  
Per Shaito et al, resveratrol may influence essential factors within cells, specifically in the cytoplasm and nucleus.\[[7](#footnote-7)] According to preliminary research, resveratrol may support the creation of new mitochondria, the cellular powerhouses responsible for energy production.\[[7](#footnote-7)] This process, known as mitochondrial biogenesis, is vital for overall cell function and energy balance.\[[7](#footnote-7)] The pathways through which resveratrol may promote mitochondrial biogenesis are the SIRT1/PGC-1α/NRF-1 and SIRT1/FoxO3a/PGC-1α pathways.\[[7](#footnote-7)] Per Shetty et al., resveratrol’s molecular action relies mainly on its binding to an enzyme named SIRT1.\[[2](#footnote-2)] The interaction between resveratrol and SIRT1 may depend on the dose, with low to moderate doses relying on SIRT1, but higher doses acting independently of SIRT1.\[[2](#footnote-2)]
Animal and in vitro studies have proposed other potential adverse events with resveratrol supplementation. An in vitro study suggested resveratrol may inhibit platelet aggregation, which may increase risk of bruising or bleeding in humans.\[[1](#footnote-1)] Concerningly, an animal study suggested that long term use of resveratrol may cause nephrotoxicity.\[[11](#footnote-11)] Further trials are needed to determine how these studies may correlate to potential adverse events in humans.  
Some researchers speculate possible drug interactions due to resveratrol’s potential to inhibit P450 cytochromes.\[[1](#footnote-1)] Per Salehi et al., due to this potential effect on cytochrome p450 activity, resveratrol may interact with drugs that use this metabolic pathway.\[[1](#footnote-1)]  
Resveratrol is not recommended for use in pregnant women.\[[8](#footnote-8)] Observations were made in animal studies concerning alteration in fetal pancreatic development when given to pregnant primates.\[[8](#footnote-8)] Avoid resveratrol supplementation during pregnancy due to potential risks to fetal development.\[[8](#footnote-8)]  
Per the Drugs and Lactation Database, there is a lack of information regarding the presence of resveratrol in breastmilk or the use of resveratrol in nursing mothers or infants.\[[9](#footnote-9)]
